main_text.l: phuris perfecti, unâ cum Mercurio absolutionis summæ.
In fronte calidum, siccum moderatè; at in recessu igneam virtutem occultans.
Eximii est splendoris, solarem imitans naturam.
Quapropter & Chymicorum Sol est, & ob igneam virtutem in abscondito, Leo ruber; in terris item humano cordi, & leoninæ naturæ consentit.
In mineralibus maximè gaudet Mercurio absolutissimo, cum quo etiam intimè commiscetur plus omnibus metallis.

Tinctúram ejus æmulantur, auripigmentum, sandaraca, sulphur fixum, præcipitatus fixus Chrysammos, (ex quo auru olim factum per additamenta quædam) & Cinnabaris (in qua Picus ait auri & argenti principia inesse) rubra stibri tinctura fixa, &c.
Argentum est metallum perfectum paulo infra aurum, albumq;[?] constans Mercurio prope fixo, & sulphure albo mundo, aliquantulum deficiente maturitate.

page.notes: The marginal note "Chymico-rum Sol & Leo ruber+" is set in italic and runs over three lines in the margin; the "+" is kept as printed. The word "albumq;" at the end of a line is doubtful: the abbreviation mark after "album" is hard to read. The Greek-style "st" ligature in "stibri" is kept as "st". The paragraph beginning "Argentum" has a decorative initial that is not a letter and is not transcribed.
